title: WebRTC connection timeout starts after potentially indefinite playback waits
test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a WebRTC start whose video.play() never settles still times out in its ICE window and falls back to the relay' and 'a viewer whose WebRTC recovery after a reconnect stalls in video.play() falls back to the relay' (chromium); tests/playbackAttempt.test.js: 'supersede gives up the attempt only while it is the current one', 'withDeadline passes the start outcome through and stops its timer', 'withDeadline gives up a start that never settles: supersedes it, frees its resources, reports a timeout', 'withDeadline leaves a newer owner alone when the attempt it guards was replaced', 'the ICE wait times out in its own window while nothing else settles', 'the ICE wait ends when the transport connects, fails or is already connected', 'the ICE wait of a transport that cleanup closed ends at once instead of waiting out its timer', 'WatchView starts WebRTC playback without waiting on video.play() before the ICE wait'
proof: Browser repro: the test stubs the viewer's HTMLMediaElement.play() to never settle for a MediaStream and makes its RTCPeerConnection use relay-only ICE (the test server offers no TURN server, so ICE can never connect), switched on after Join. Test 1 clicks Watch on a direct (non-tunnel) viewer; test 2 first plays over WebRTC, then drops the viewer's WebSocket so the reconnect recovery restarts WebRTC. Both expect the viewer to reach 'relay mode active' (the fallback after the 8 s ICE timeout) well before 25 s / 30 s, with no alert and the room at relayViewerCount 1 / mediasoupConsumerCount 0. On the unchanged code (dev 437b8f2, whole media-flow spec, run-e2e.cjs --workers=1; scratchpad watch-TASK-088-before-media-flow.txt) both failed: the page stayed on a disabled 'Connecting...' button for the whole 25 s / 30 s window (consumeProducer awaited play(), so the ICE wait was never installed; handleWatch's 40 s safety timer would have ended test 1 later with 'Connection timed out', and nothing ever ended the recovery in test 2). The other 13 tests of the spec passed there (the base baseline); the run's 16th test, 'capture denial ...', failed only because the two failed tests left their rooms active (rooms.active 1), and the 17th (autoplay denial) passed. After the fix the whole spec passes 17 of 17 (watch-TASK-088-after-media-flow.txt) and the two new tests take 11.4 s and 12.5 s (8 s ICE window + relay start); 3 of 3 with --repeat-each=3 (watch-TASK-088-after-repeat.txt). Fix: consumeProducer starts playVideoElement without awaiting it (no await on play() remains on the mediasoup start path; the autoplay-denial muted retry still runs inside playVideoElement and the existing autoplay test passes); the ICE wait is waitForTransportConnected in src/lib/playbackAttempt.mjs (same 2 s/8 s values and messages; it also ends at once when cleanupPlayback closes the transport, which mediasoup-client reports only on transport.observer); withDeadline (40 s) wraps handleTryMediasoup and the WebRTC start of the transport-failed and reconnect recoveries and, at the deadline, supersedes a still-current attempt, releases its own resources and rejects with PlaybackDeadlineError (an attempt a newer owner replaced rejects as superseded instead). A browser test of the 40 s deadline itself is not feasible: Try WebRTC exists only in OBS fallback mode (no OBS in the test server), and the recovery's WebRTC start now ends at its ICE window long before 40 s, so the deadline is covered by unit tests with a short ms. Verification: node --test tests/playbackAttempt.test.js tests/subscriptionLedger.test.js 25/25; npm run lint and typecheck clean; npm test 1388/1388.
